claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can be used to assess whether the alloy has a ferromagnetic ground state.
A ferromagnetic ground state is indicated when the computed ferromagnetic configuration has lower total energy than the corresponding nonmagnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations.
The proposed material is a disordered Al0.1CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy or a similar transition-metal alloy.
Several magnetic configurations should be evaluated using spin-polarized first-principles DFT.
The calculations are to be performed at 0 K.
Local chemical disorder should be included in the calculations where possible.
Local atomic arrangements and clustering may mediate exchange interactions between transition-metal atoms.
Favorable exchange interactions among transition-metal d electrons can produce spin splitting.
Spin splitting can lower the total energy of ferromagnetic alignment.
A ferromagnetic ground state results when the energy gain from ferromagnetic alignment exceeds that available from antiferromagnetic or nonmagnetic ordering.
The ferromagnetic configuration is predicted to have lower total energy than the nonmagnetic and antiferromagnetic states.
The ferromagnetic configuration is predicted to have finite magnetization per atom.
The exchange-correlation functional, treatment of chemical disorder, and omission of finite-temperature effects introduce uncertainty into the predicted magnetic ordering.
The precise energy differences and their sensitivity to local chemical order are not specified and require further calculations.
